messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert -> GPU inference pool (us-west-2) queue growth detected. 90th p99 latency spike, ~30% 503s, HPA replicas not increasing. Possible metrics pipeline lag (prom-adapter). Paging oncall.

maya: on it. Confirming customer impact?

incident-bot: Customers: multiple prod tenants experiencing timeouts on generate endpoints. Error rate up ~28% over last 3m. Queue length: 340 requests.

maya: ok reassigning. @aj can you pull adapter logs and HPA status?

aj: looking. quick checks: 
```
kubectl get hpa -n inference
NAME           REFERENCE                  TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-hpa  Deployment/inference-svc   0%/80%    2         50        2          14d
```
HPA still at 2, but CPU/req metrics on prometheus show request rate to pods > target. Prom-adapter reports backlog.

aj: grabbing prom-adapter logs now.

aj: log excerpt: 
```
E0305 18:02:12.123 prom-adapter metrics_ingest.go:312] scrape queue backlog size=12000, worker_pool=5, dropping samples=true
W0305 18:02:14.987 adapter server: heartbeat missed to metrics-server
```

aj: prom-adapter pod OOM recently? Checking events.

maya: can we see metrics-server and prometheus scrape latency?

aj: prometheus remote writes fine. Scrape latencies: node exporters ok, but custom HPA targets appear delayed by ~2m. metrics-server shows spike in scrape duration.

infra-bot: Alert -> prom-adapter high queue depth (pod/prom-adapter-2) CPU throttling.

maya: hypothesis: prom-adapter slowed -> HPA custom metrics not updated -> HPA didn't scale -> GPU pool exhausted -> queue growth & throttling. Mitigate: 1) manual scale replicas; 2) add temporary rate limit; 3) route some traffic to fallback region.

leo: I'll take manual scale. Scaling inference deployment to 20 now.

aj: manual scale command: 
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-svc --replicas=20
```

aj: also bumping prom-adapter replicas to 4 and restarting the problematic pod.

maya: customer-ops, please prepare comms: ETA for recovery? list of affected tenants?

customer-ops: compiling list. Notifying top 5 paying tenants, internal status page updated.

sara: adding temporary global token rate limiter to reduce further queue buildup. Pushing patch to gateway.

aj: prom-adapter pod restarted. queue depth dropping in logs: 
```
I0305 18:06:05.210 metrics_ingest.go:178] processed 4800 samples, backlog=200
I0305 18:06:20.412 metrics_ingest.go:178] processed 1800 samples, backlog=0
```

aj: HPA custom metrics appear to be updating now. watching.

leo: HPA observed new metrics and started scaling: 
```
Events:
  Normal  SuccessfulRescale  2m (x1 over 2m)  horizontal-pod-autoscaler  New size: 20; reason: CPU threshold
```

maya: traffic still elevated but error rate falling. current queue length ~40.

customer-ops: customers reporting degraded but functional. some timeouts resolved.

maya: handing off to night oncall @leo with summary: prom-adapter experienced CPU throttling causing scrape/backlog and metrics delay. manual scale + prom-adapter patch + gateway rate limiting mitigated visible impact. followups: 1) root cause investigation on prom-adapter OOM/throttling under burst; 2) add circuit-breaker to HPA targets to avoid single-point adapter; 3) test cross-region failover automation; 4) postmortem.

leo: acknowledged, taking over. I've created an incident follow-up ticket INF-9876.

maya: thanks team. marking the incident as mitigated but not resolved. will reconvene for postmortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:
